messages:
Alex: Quick check — I'm seeing mismatches between per-invocation token cost in the console vs our sampled telemetry. screenshot: https://redwood.internal/s/abc123 :eyes:
Maya: hmm, do you mean the per-request card or the rollout preview panel?
Alex: rollout preview mainly, but it shows ~30% more cost than the aggregated sample in billing.
Priya: is this the cache-crediting path? we recently changed how shared prefetched KV is amortized
Alex: possible. Also looks like some invocations report 0 tokens (cache-hit-only) and still show cost in the preview.
Jordan: can you paste the exact sample query you used? I want to check sampling window alignment
Alex: sure: ``SELECT route, count(*) as calls, sum(tokens) as tokens FROM telemetry WHERE ts>now()-1h SAMPLE 1/100``
Sam: big clue: our sample pipeline drops requests with 0 token payloads (we treat them as ping) so the aggregator undercounts cache-only invocations
Maya: so console is including amortized cache cost while sampled telemetry excludes those events.
Priya: that's a product decision — console should surface both: `visible_cost` (what customer will see) and `measured_econ` (sampled telemetry). UX needs to label them clearly
Jordan: implementation debate: do we add a `cost_estimate` field on the internal route-summary API (cheap, avoids double-joins) or compute in the console by joining two endpoints?
Sam: adding `cost_estimate` to the route-summary API seems fine but it requires us to pick a canonical amortization algorithm. messy for multi-model chains
Priya: for multi-model chains we should expose breakdown per model SKU and a slab credit line. otherwise users misinterpret the uplift
Alex: agreed. But performance: computing that at read-time for every route-summary request will be heavy. we need a sampled precompute job or materialized view
Maya: what if we precompute per-epoch amortized credits and store them with the route-sku mapping, then console does an extra join? tradeoff: storage vs CPU.
Jordan: +1 for epoch precompute. Also we can tag the preview toggle with a sample-confidence badge based on sample rate
Sam: operational note: if we change sample behavior to include 0-token cache-hits, ingestion QPS will rise ~2-4%. Ops wants a flag to gate it and a rollout plan
Alex: can we prototype a gated pipeline toggle? I can add a canary job that flips for 5% of routes.
Priya: UX asks: add a tooltip "Includes amortized cache credits" and a small example calc. Non-ambiguous labeling is key.
Maya: dev-labs idea: in rollout preview show both numbers side-by-side and expose a button: "explain difference" which opens a short trace linking to sampled telemetry slices
Jordan: code sketch for precompute job:
```
INSERT INTO amortized_credits(epoch, route, sku, credit)
SELECT epoch, route, sku, sum(prefetch_cost)/count(distinct session_id)
FROM prefetch_events
WHERE epoch = $E
GROUP BY epoch, route, sku;
```
we run every 15m for hot epochs.
Sam: ops +1 if it's bounded and backfill-friendly. Also we should emit a telemetry event when the UI shows a sampled-vs-precomputed diff > 20% so we can triage regressions
cost-bot: [alert] precompute-job latency increased 30% at 1709999980 — investigating
Alex: thanks. next steps: Maya + Priya to draft UX copy and mock side-by-side numbers. Jordan + Sam to prototype epoch precompute as a gated canary (5% routes). I'll own the "explain difference" trace link
Maya: I'll put mocks in Figma and add microcopy suggestions.
Priya: I'll draft spec for multi-model breakdown and a tooltip bank.
Jordan: I'll spin up the precompute PoC and push a feature-flagged endpoint.
Sam: I'll add ingestion toggle and a metric for sample-confidence. Ops will approve after canary metrics look stable.
Alex: great — ping me when the flag is ready and I'll validate numbers end-to-end. :thumbsup:
